designs.candidate: Deferred — CVE severity enrichment with evidence-cited retrieval and explicit abstention

kill_shots.flaw: The entire pre-registered success bar is cleared by a ONE-LINE constant with no LLM, no tools, no retrieval, no cost and no human time. I rebuilt the eval pool from the NVD API and confirmed every claimed number to the decimal (n=167, APY 9.0% = 15/167, band 48.5%, DUR 37.1%, >=2 bands 7.8%, over-rating 14.4%, and all 8 per-metric and all 8 majority-class cells). Then I tested the obvious rule the design never ran: take the CNA vector and overwrite AC with LOW. Result on the identical 167 cases: APY 23.4%, DUR 25.7%, coverage 100%. The pre-registered bar is APY >= 18.0%, DUR <= 30.0%, coverage >= 75%. The one-liner passes all three simultaneously. Adding a second constant (S:=UNCHANGED) gives APY 26.3% / DUR 30.5%. An exhaustive search over all 256 fixed CNA-vs-majority hybrids confirms 26.3% is the optimum, and it is not overfit: it holds on two disjoint windows (Jan 2025 n=495: 23.4% -> 35.6%; Aug 2026 n=47 fully held out: 14.9% -> 31.9%). The design's shipped 'deliberately STRONG' baseline — a per-CWE precedent lookup with >=5 support and >=90% purity — scores 13.2%, i.e. HALF what two constants achieve. The sentence 'I report the agent against the harder of the two, so a weak-baseline accusation has nothing to land on' is exactly inverted.
kill_shots.why_fatal: Measured Improvement is 15 points and the improvement is measured against a bar a judge beats in 90 seconds — using a table the submission itself prints. The design publishes 'AC: CNA 65.3% vs majority-class 88.6%' in its own per-metric results and even writes that 'the AC skill's job is mostly to resist inventing complexity.' It identified the ingredient and never combined it. Any judge reading that row asks 'so why not just use the majority for AC?' and the answer is a 14.4-point APY jump. Second barrel on baseline fairness, which the brief says judges are explicitly instructed to check: the status-quo CNA baseline is 23.4% on the Jan 2025 window the project uses for its hot take, versus 9.0% on the July 2026 window it evaluates on. The project's own two datasets disagree about whether 18% is even an improvement — on Jan 2025 the untouched status quo already beats the agent's target. A 9.0% headline baseline reads as a window chosen to make the starting point look maximally weak, which is precisely the 'baseline set up to fail' pattern the strategy brief flags as a scoring liability.
kill_shots.fixable: Yes, cheaply and immediately, but it costs the headline. Adopt the two-constant rule (26.3% APY / 30.5% DUR) as Arm B, delete the 13.2% precedent script or demote it to a changelog negative result, and re-pre-register the target above it — realistically APY >= 33% with DUR <= 25%. Do this BEFORE H5, because after the agent exists it looks like moving the goalposts. Also report the status quo on all three windows so the 9.0% figure cannot be read as cherry-picked. The honest consequence: the target roughly doubles in difficulty and Kill Shot 3 says the LLM makes the residual worse, so the probability of a positive headline drops sharply. This is a real fix, not a free one.

kill_shots.flaw: The hot take — the project's signature 5-point insight — collapses on the project's own evaluation set. The claim is that expert-disagreement corpora are dominated by template collisions: '45.1% sit inside a triple repeated five or more times, 47 of Cisco Talos's 60 divergences are one identical S:U-vs-S:C delta.' I verified this exactly on Jan 2025: 379 divergent, 181 distinct (CNA, NVD-vector, CNA-vector) triples, 171 cases (45.1%) in >=5x templates, Talos x47. I then ran the identical check on the July 2026 pool the project actually evaluates on: 152 divergent cases, 122 distinct triples, and only 10 cases (6.6%) in a >=5x template. The largest single pattern is x5. Cisco Talos does not appear in the top 12 assigners of the eval pool at all. Divergence in the eval window is ~80% idiosyncratic, not template-driven.
kill_shots.why_fatal: The hot take is measured on a corpus the submission does not use and does not hold on the corpus it does. Worse, the design hands the judge the weapon: it states the check 'costs one Counter over source-plus-vector-pair triples.' A judge who takes that invitation and runs it against the shipped data/ directory gets 6.6%, not 45.1%, and now doubts every other number — which is unfair, because every other number is exactly right, but that is how credibility works. It also removes the stated rationale for the stratified 120-case sample ('the direct lesson of the template-collision finding'), which is now solving a problem absent from its own eval set. And there is a third-order cost: no dominant templates means precedent retrieval has far less structure to exploit, making the APY target harder, not easier.
kill_shots.fixable: Yes, and the fix is strictly better than the original. Reframe it as a longitudinal finding: templates dominated CNA/NVD divergence in Jan 2025 (45.1%) and have largely dissolved by Jul 2026 (6.6%) — measured, same script, two windows, both shipped. That is a more interesting and more defensible claim than the static one, it keeps the generalisable lesson ('deduplicate disagreement before you benchmark, and re-run the check per window because the answer moves'), and it costs one paragraph plus a table. Do NOT move the eval to Jan 2025 to rescue the original framing — that would destroy the post-cutoff contamination story, which is one of the design's genuine strengths.

kill_shots.flaw: The agent's LLM component is documented — by the design's own cited prior art — to underperform the incumbent on exactly the metrics that dominate the remaining error. After the two-constant fix, I profiled the residual on the 167: 44 cases already exact, then PR-only 14, A-only 14, S-only 10, C/I/A together 8, AC 6, UI 5. So PR and A are the two largest single-metric buckets. The design cites arXiv 2512.06781 as its 'published weak external baseline,' reporting GPT-5 scoring from description alone at 71.6% on Privileges Required and 68.0% on Availability Impact. On this pool the CNA the agent is overriding already achieves 83.2% PR and 71.9% A. The agent's per-metric judgement is therefore expected to move both dominant residual buckets backwards.
kill_shots.why_fatal: The design presents that paper as supporting evidence ('the authors name the missing ingredient as context — which is precisely what an agent adds'), but read against this pool it is a prediction of failure. It strips the agent down to one credible lever: precedent retrieval. And precedent retrieval is the lookup table the project's own hot take indicts as something that 'scores like domain reasoning, generalises like a lookup table.' The 30-point Agent Solution row asks 'which design choices helped the agent solve the problem' — and after this analysis the honest answer is 'two constants did most of it, and the one agentic capability with headroom is the one my hot take warns against.' The per-case oracle over {CNA value, majority class} is 69.5%, so headroom genuinely exists, but nothing in the design demonstrates the agent can reach into it.
kill_shots.fixable: Partially. Restrict the agent to a gated adjudicator: it may only override a metric where retrieved precedent clears a support and purity threshold, and must ACCEPT otherwise — never free-form scoring from the description. That protects PR and A from LLM degradation and turns the comparison into a clean ablation. But it converges the agent toward the script, shrinking the agentic contribution toward zero and making the compute-matched control (which already gets the same k=12 precedents in-prompt) very hard to beat. Also drop the 8 per-metric skill files to 3 — AV (95.2%), AC (constant) and S (constant) do not need skills; PR, C/I/A and the abstention policy do. That is component inflation the PDF penalises by name, and cutting it buys back roughly 2 hours.

kill_shots.flaw: The evaluation population is the systematic inverse of the target population, and the effect is sharper than the design's self-assessment admits. Eligibility requires an NVD analyst vector, so the eval set is by construction the CVEs NVD chose to analyse — while the product exists to serve the ones it deferred. I quantified the amplification: for Aug 1-20 2026, totalResults is 9,003, only 342 of the 2,000 on page 1 are Analyzed, 47 are eval-eligible, and every one of those 47 was published in week 1 (Aug 1-7). Nothing published after Aug 7 has been analysed at all. So eligibility is not merely 'NVD analysed it' — it is 'NVD analysed it fastest,' and since the April 2026 policy NVD triages by KEV membership, active exploitation and vendor prominence. The labelled set is the rushed-to-the-front slice of the queue.
kill_shots.why_fatal: Both headline numbers are statements about a population defined by the opposite of the selection rule that creates the user's problem. DUR 37.1% -> target <=30.0% is the emotional core of the pitch ('trusting the shipped number silently under-rates better than one CVE in three'), and it is measured only where NVD sprinted. Andrew Maas — the best available proxy judge, who built the IMDB benchmark — is exactly the reader who spots this in the first minute, and the brief warns eval-set construction is what he scrutinises hardest. The design names it third in its self-assessment and calls it 'least fixable,' which is correct and earns real honesty credit, but honesty does not restore the measurement.
kill_shots.fixable: No, not eliminable — but it is boundable, cheaply, and the robustness check would impress precisely the judge most likely to raise it. Compute days-from-publication-to-analysis for every eval case (both fields are in the record you already have) and report APY and DUR stratified into fast-analysed versus slow-analysed tertiles. If the metrics are flat across tertiles, you have real evidence the labelled set is not merely the easy tail; if they degrade with lag, you have measured the direction and size of your own selection bias and can state a bound instead of a caveat. Roughly 30 minutes of work using data already in the snapshot, and it converts the weakest disclosure in the submission into a demonstration of benchmark craft.

survivable_weaknesses: All published distributions are page-1 statistics presented as window statistics. The July window has totalResults 5,479 but only 2,000 were fetched; August has 9,003 with 2,000 fetched. The vulnStatus split (1,026 Deferred / 795 Analyzed) and the '82% of her queue' headline are computed on the earliest 2,000 of 5,479 — which, being oldest, are the MOST likely to have been enriched. The true deferral rate across the full window is probably higher, so the error runs in the pitch's favour. Fix by paginating (3 requests for July, 5 for August) and restating. Cheap, and leaving it unfixed is an unforced credibility hole given how good the rest of the data work is.

Minor count discrepancies I could not reconcile: the design claims 365 NVD Primary vectors and 1,960 CNA vectors; I get 357 NVD-primary v3.1 and 1,648 non-NVD v3.1, but exactly 1,960 CNA and 358 NVD when counting across all CVSS versions. So the 1,960 figure requires an any-version count while the surrounding analysis is v3.1-only. The 82% headline survives, but state the version filter explicitly or a checker will think the numbers wobble.

Repo weight versus the offline-reproduction promise. The precedent index (2024-06 to 2025-06) is roughly 40,000 CVEs — I measured 9,292 in a single three-month slice — which is approximately 150 MB of byte-verbatim raw JSON. 'Committed byte-verbatim' collides with 'a judge clones and runs it offline.' The NVD terms only forbid attributing MODIFIED content to NVD; they do not require verbatim vendoring. Ship the precedent index gzipped or field-pruned under data/derived/ with the derived header, and keep byte-verbatim vendoring for the 120-case test set and its vulnrichment records only.

The NVD terms page returns HTTP 403 to fetchers (I reproduced this), so the licence section rests on a Wayback snapshot. The design already flags a browser re-check as a gate action — keep it, and record the date checked in the README as planned. Separately: https://www.cve.org/Legal/TermsOfUse now returns HTTP 200, contradicting the claim that it has no readable version — but it is a JavaScript shell with no server-rendered text, so the conservative decision to design cvelistV5 out remains correct. Do not reopen that dependency at hour 20.

The output artifact is opaque on video. 'CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H' means nothing to a judge who is not a vulnerability manager, and 20 points ride partly on whether the intended user would consider the output high quality. The per-metric evidence table with cited spans and a recomputed score is genuinely good raw material — but the video must lead with the human-legible layer (this CVE moves from MEDIUM to HIGH, here is the metric that moved it, here is the sentence that justifies it, here is the one we handed back) rather than the vector string. The author's admitted non-expert status is a real risk here: get a practitioner to read the README before recording, as already planned.

The submission forfeits an empty lane while paying its costs. The strategy brief verifies zero occupancy for 'abstention as the PRIMARY metric.' This design makes abstention a side-channel scored as zero on APY, so it pays the full APY tax (at the pre-registered 75% coverage floor, the agent must hit 24% on answered cases just to show 18% overall — 2.7x the status quo) while claiming none of the differentiation. The design also concedes abstention is its least-finished component, its one deterministic trigger measurably failed to stratify (8.7/15.4/6.2/8.3%), and it will likely fall back on model self-report — the introspective machinery micro1's CEO is on record doubting. Either build the calibration story properly (selective-risk / risk-coverage curve, which is deterministic and would claim the empty lane) or cut abstention entirely and reclaim the coverage. Half-building it is the worst of both.

Genuine assets that should survive any rewrite, and should be defended loudly: I independently reimplemented the CVSS v3.1 formula and reproduced all 334 published base scores in the eval pool with zero mismatches, corroborating the 4,380/4,380 claim — the verifier is real, closed-form and load-bearing rather than decorative. The removed experiment is already run and genuinely instructive (CISA Technical Impact shows a five-fold lift, 73.1% vs 14.2%, and still loses to the incumbent on all three metrics it targets, because the baseline already conditions on the same evidence). The offline harness with a no-socket pytest, the SHA256 manifest, the dev/test split touched twice, and the CC0 vulnrichment licence (I read the LICENSE file: 'Creative Commons Legal Code / CC0 1.0 Universal') are all solid. The bottleneck is real and government-announced. Reproducibility is the strongest row and should stay that way.

designs.candidate: Bindline — consistency-under-precedent for HTSUS tariff classification

kill_shots.flaw: The declared BIND selection rule produces basket-code coincidences, not repeated merchandise — so memory is inert on the majority of the primary metric. I rebuilt the rule against live CROSS data (388 in-scope NY rulings, 49 code-groups with >=2 rulings). The largest group, 3924.90.5650 (40 rulings), contains a plastic rake, a scrub sponge, a pail, a bucket, a birdfeeder, a plastic sterilizer bag, a fly swatter and a 'Skeleton King Nutcracker Greeter'. 6912.00.4810 (10 rulings) spans a shot glass, popcorn bowls, spice containers, cookie cutters and a candy bowl. 4419.90.9100 (7) spans cutting boards, a placemat, a serving tray, a utensil holder and a wood tray.
kill_shots.why_fatal: BIND pairs are defined as 'CBP assigned the identical 10-digit code', which for residual 'Other' provisions means two unrelated goods that happen to converge on a catch-all. The Classification Decision Register keys on commodity profile; a fly swatter and a nutcracker share no profile, so the register never fires and A1 is byte-identical to C1 on those pairs. The flagship capability cannot move the flagship metric on its dominant bucket. Worse, the design faces a closed dilemma: follow the pre-declared rule literally and CUP-BIND gain is ~0, or hand-curate BIND down to genuinely similar goods and the pre-declared rule plus the 'no pair is dropped' policy are both abandoned — making selection the entire mechanism of the result rather than a confessed caveat. A judge who runs the published query finds this in 15 minutes.
kill_shots.fixable: Partially, and expensively. Redefine BIND as 'same 10-digit code AND commodity-profile overlap above a stated threshold', or scope the entire corpus to one narrow family where the codes are not baskets — 3924.10.4000 (28 rulings) is mostly genuine drinkware and would survive. But a tumbler-only 36-line queue reads as a toy, and either fix means re-deriving the pair set after H5, which the 26h plan has no room for.

kill_shots.flaw: CUP-BIND decomposes into accuracy plus consistent-wrongness, and the memory-attributable half is the half the domain's own legal framing condemns.
kill_shots.why_fatal: Because BIND pairs are constructed as pairs where CBP assigned the same code, P(BIND satisfied) = P(both correct) + P(both wrong identically). There is no third cell. So the CUP-BIND lift attributable to memory net of accuracy is exactly the rate at which the agent propagates a wrong code to a later line. The README argues that reasonable care under 19 U.S.C. 1484 obliges consistency with prior treatment and with CBP's binding rulings — i.e. consistency with the correct answer — and that ACE surfaces drift into Form 28/29/1592 exposure. Repeating one wrong code across two lines of the same entry is a compounding violation whose penalty scales with the number of affected lines, not a virtue. The primary metric rewards the precise behaviour the value proposition calls dangerous. This is a 90-second observation for any judge who reads the metric definition next to the legal argument, and it lands on the integrity claim the whole submission is staked on.
kill_shots.fixable: Not without killing the thesis. Scoring BIND as 'consistent AND both correct' fixes the inversion but collapses CUP into accuracy-squared, at which point 'memory is the thesis' is decorative — which is the design's own stated biggest_risk, arriving structurally rather than empirically.

kill_shots.flaw: The eval's difficulty is authored by the contestant, and check_leakage.py cannot detect the leakage that matters. Queue lines are 'the ruling's own factual merchandise description reformatted into invoice-line style', but a CROSS facts section is written after the holding and recites the facts the National Import Specialist found dispositive, in the legal test's own vocabulary.
kill_shots.why_fatal: I read the two headline hard cases in full. N355970 states 'a double-walled receptacle with no vacuum properties' and 'plastic components are the predominant material by weight and value' — that second sentence IS the GRI 3(b) essential-character holding, pre-digested. N356922 states 'the space between the two walls was not filled with insulating material' and 'a double-walled, vacuum insulated vessel' — which is heading 9617's own terms ('Vacuum flasks and other vacuum vessels'). N363968 writes 'acacia wood (Acacia spp., a tropical wood)' where 4419.20 is literally 'of tropical wood'. Keep those facts and the split is a keyword match any model wins with no memory; strip them and the pair becomes unanswerable rather than hard. check_leakage.py only asserts no HTS-shaped 4+ digit string survives — it is blind to this entire class. Separately, the claimed minimal pairs are not minimal: N355970 is a plastic-predominant PP/steel composite and N356922 is an all-stainless vacuum vessel; N333570 is a bare alder board and N363968 is a multi-component board system with steel strainer, bins and rack requiring GRI 3(b). 'One word of difference' is the contestant's invoice-line rewrite, not a property of the goods. The hard case is manufactured, and the manufacturer is the person being graded.
kill_shots.fixable: Only by writing invoice lines from supplier-style commercial language rather than from CBP's facts section — which requires domain judgement the author has already conceded he lacks, and reintroduces authored difficulty from the other direction. There is no clean escape: the facts section is the only merchandise text CROSS provides.

kill_shots.flaw: The baseline is the strongest possible system on the primary metric, and the modal outcome is no measurable gain. B0 receives all 36 lines in one context window and returns 36 codes in one pass.
kill_shots.why_fatal: Batch-in-one-window is the best-known way to get an LLM to self-align across similar items; B0 can trivially notice lines 6 and 24 describe the same tumbler because it sees them simultaneously. Meanwhile CUP-SPLIT is likely near-ceiling for every arm, because the real splits are either chapter-level and keyword-obvious (a stainless-steel cutting board at 7323.93.0060 versus a wood one at 4419.x) or statistical-suffix coin flips at 10 digits that nobody wins reliably. So the plausible result matrix is B0 ~ C1 ~ A1 on both buckets, inside per-run spread. At n~18 BIND pairs a 10-point pre-registered gain is 1.8 pairs. The design names this ('if B0 wins CUP-BIND, that is the finding') and has no fallback metric, no second corpus and no reserve hours. Measured Improvement is 15 points and the third tie-break; arriving at H21 with a null on the primary metric and 5 hours of write-up left is the single most likely path through this plan.
kill_shots.fixable: Yes in principle, badly in practice. A structurally stateless baseline restores the gap but is exactly the rigged baseline the brief says gets punished hardest, and the design already rejected it for that reason. Seeding the register from prior entries (making memory cross-entry rather than within-invoice, which is also the truer bottleneck) would restore a real asymmetry, but that is a different eval design, not a patch.

kill_shots.flaw: 'I select which pairs enter the set; I do not author a single label' is false for a material share of the corpus, and it is the sentence the integrity claim rests on.
kill_shots.why_fatal: Measured on the live API over the design's own scope: 42% of in-scope NY rulings (163/388) carry Chapter-99 overlay codes in the tariffs field — N355970 returns '3924.10.4000, 9903.01.24, 9903.01.25' — so a contestant-authored rule decides that 9903.* is stripped and the first code is primary. 17% (67/388) carry more than one distinct substantive code, and the API supplies no code-to-product mapping: N338282 is 'a ceramic cup and a plastic tumbler' returning '3924.10.4000, 6912.00.4500, 9817.95.05', so which code is the gold label for which line is the contestant's call. Others carry 9817.95.05 (festive articles) and 9801.00.1098 (US goods returned), each needing another authored rule. Additionally, verify_labels.py's 'two independent fields' are the search API's tariffs field and the 'TARIFF NO.:' line inside the same ruling — one source rendered twice, not two sources, so the cross-check cannot detect the failure mode it implies. Being caught overclaiming on integrity is worse than having no integrity section, and this design invites the check by publishing the exact endpoint.
kill_shots.fixable: Yes, cheaply, and it should be done regardless: scope to single-substantive-code rulings only. That drops roughly a fifth of the corpus, which 388 in-scope rulings can absorb, and the honest sentence becomes 'I normalise Chapter-99 overlays by a stated rule and exclude multi-product rulings for that reason.' Costs about 40 minutes and removes the whole attack.

kill_shots.flaw: The guard metric is measured at chapter level while the primary metric is scored at 10 digits, leaving an open gaming lane between them.
kill_shots.why_fatal: A degenerate policy of 'answer the modal 10-digit code within the correct chapter' raises CUP-BIND, is invisible to a chapter-level agreement guard, and does not touch CUP-SPLIT@4 or @6 — which the live data suggests are where most real splits sit (3924 vs 9617 diverges at digit one; 4419.20 vs 4419.90 at digit six). Only CUP-SPLIT@10 pushes back, and those are the noisiest pairs in the set. The design's central anti-degeneracy argument — 'the two axes oppose each other by construction, both must be won at once' — does not hold at the resolution where the gaming happens. The headline hard case (3924 vs 9617) is also a chapter split, so it is scored once in CUP-SPLIT@4 and again in the guard: the guard and the primary metric are not independent, which is exactly what a guard is for.
kill_shots.fixable: Yes. Guard at 6 digits with a wider tolerance band, or add a code-entropy floor (no arm may concentrate more than k% of outputs on one 10-digit code). Both are under an hour and both should ship.

survivable_weaknesses: Lane emptiness is real and is the design's best asset. My own census returned 0 repos for tariff/HTS/customs classification agents created since kickoff, against 36 repos mentioning micro1; the strategy brief's 'regulated non-software domains ~0 of 64' held under independent probe. Whatever else is wrong, the 15-point Problem row is uncontested.

Every data, licence and reachability claim checks out exactly as stated. CROSS search 200 (42,777 bytes), all four cited rulings 200, USITC ch.44 200 at 276,836 bytes, CBP copyright notice returns the public-domain sentence verbatim, robots.txt 404. The corpus is bigger than claimed (388 in-scope NY rulings from 24 calls, versus 183 asserted). No licence landmine, no account, no click-through. This clears ground rules 03 and 07 cleanly.

Reproducibility is close to best-in-field: vendored snapshot with SHA-256 manifest, offline execution, dependency-free stdlib scorer with no model in the path, pinned versions, exact commands for all three arms. This is the second tie-break criterion and it is genuinely strong.
Cost per task and human time per task instrumented from H7, before the first real run. The brief verified only two repos on GitHub carry both phrases. Near-free differentiation, correctly sequenced.

The removed experiment (precedent-first retrieval) is well chosen — lexical similarity as an anti-signal at the classification boundary is a real and teachable finding, and the fallback removal candidate is pre-registered so the changelog cannot end up all-wins.

The hot take ('ship the overrule before you ship the recall') is specific, transferable and turns a failure mode into a build rule, which is literally what the 5-point row asks for. It is asserted as already-measured when the runs have not happened, but as a claim it is defensible.

Human time per task is n=5, self-timed, by a non-LCB, on cases whose gold answers the author personally derived from the source rulings. This is not merely soft — it is contaminated by knowledge of the answer. Disclosing it as soft does not fix the contamination, but it is a small share of the score.

Adjacency to micro1's Realm Tax benchmark is a real but second-order risk. Tariff nomenclature is a distinct discipline; the exposure is that a judge who owns Realm Tax reads Bindline against in-house work. Confessed openly, which is the right handling.

Expected 10-digit agreement of 20-35% across all arms means the worksheet an LCB receives is wrong at the filing-relevant level roughly two times in three. Printing it low is honest and correctly anticipated, but it caps the End-to-End Quality row, since the answer to 'would the intended user consider this high quality' is that she would not file it unreviewed.

designs.candidate: Second Analyst — coding NASA ASRS free-text aviation-safety narratives into the Primary Problem / Contributing Factors taxonomy, with Ambiguous treated as abstention

kill_shots.flaw: The "invariant I discovered in the data" is the definition of the ASRS coding form, not a discovery. I pulled NASA's own ASRS Coding Form (https://asrs.arc.nasa.gov/docs/dbol/ASRS_CodingTaxonomy.pdf, page 16, April 2024). Under 'Assessments' it prints 'Contributing Factors / Situations' as a checklist of ~15 categories, and directly beneath it 'Primary Problem' as the SAME category list plus one extra option: Ambiguous. I confirmed this against his own corpus: CF vocabulary = 16 values, PP vocabulary = 17 values, and the set difference is exactly {Ambiguous}, in both directions. Primary Problem is a single-select from the contributing-factors checklist with an 'I can't pick' escape hatch. That is why it holds 1354/1354 = 100.00%.
kill_shots.why_fatal: It is the justification for one of only three capabilities, and it is the load-bearing claim behind the 'mathematically derived failure taxonomy'. A judge who opens one public NASA PDF sees that the 100.00% is a tautology of a form, presented as an empirical finding — which reframes the whole submission's rigour as credulous rather than careful. Downstream it makes the verifier near-decorative: it checks that the agent's Primary Problem appears in the agent's OWN Contributing Factors list, so it validates self-consistency between two of the model's own outputs, never correctness. Tell the model 'pick the primary from the list you just wrote' (or emit an index into that array) and the violation rate is ~0 at baseline, so F5 ≈ 0, the bounded re-code never fires, and Iteration 3 measures nothing. It is also the single most crowded pattern in the field per the strategy brief (§2.2, 'deterministic verification wrapped around a model' is now the field's median move).
kill_shots.fixable: Yes, cheaply, but the fix costs him a capability. Stop claiming discovery: cite the coding form, say the constraint is definitional, and keep the check as a one-line schema guarantee rather than an 'iteration'. Then either drop to two capabilities (Skill + retrieval), which the PDF explicitly rewards ('purposeful choices matter more than the number of components'), or repoint verification at something the form does NOT guarantee — e.g. that every emitted Contributing Factor has a supporting evidence span that actually occurs verbatim in the whitelisted input, which is checkable by string operations, is NOT definitional, and will genuinely fire.

kill_shots.flaw: His topic-disjoint split turns BM25 precedent retrieval — the capability he calls 'the one most likely to carry the result' — into a majority-class amplifier. I implemented it (pure-Python BM25, k1=1.5, b=0.75, over narratives) on his exact 9-eval-set / 21-exemplar-set split and measured it. The eval pool's true label rate is Human Factors 27.5% / Ambiguous 17.6%. The label prior of the top-5 retrieved precedents is Human Factors 38.6% / Ambiguous 11.0%. So the precedent context is biased +11.1 points toward the majority class and −6.6 points against the abstention class the entire product thesis rests on. Per-class recall of the true label anywhere in the top-5: Human Factors 94.0%, Aircraft 86.5%, Weather 73.9% — but Airport 0/11, Chart Or Publication 0/6, Software and Automation 0/5, Manuals 0/3, Airspace Structure 1/13 (7.7%), ATC Equipment 1/11 (9.1%), Environment–Non Weather 4/30 (13.3%). BM25 kNN majority vote scores 35.3% @k=5 against a 27.5% constant predictor.
kill_shots.why_fatal: Retrieval works ~94% of the time on the class he must NOT drift toward and ~0–13% of the time on the long tail his guard metric protects. His own pre-registered guard ('long-tail agreement must not fall below the single-prompt baseline on the same subset') is therefore positioned to reject his flagship capability. Worse, it lands on the demo: for ACN 2028890 — the hard case the video, the hot take and the F1/F2 story are all built on — the top-5 retrieved precedents are ['Human Factors','Human Factors','Procedure','Human Factors','Human Factors'] and the true label (ATC Equipment / Nav Facility / Buildings) is not retrieved at all. The retriever feeds the model the wrong answer four times out of five on the exact case whose lesson is 'beware the salient Human Factors reading'. The cause is mechanical, not bad luck: he chose the 9 eval sets by LOWEST majority-class concentration, which by construction leaves the 21 exemplar sets more concentrated (constant predictor 43.9% on exemplars vs 27.5% on eval), and the rare classes have almost no exemplars to retrieve (ATC Equipment 6, Software 5, Chart 5, Manuals 2, Staffing 1 across the whole 986-record pool).
kill_shots.fixable: Yes, and the fix is better than the original — but only if he finds it before H11, and only one variant preserves his H4 freeze. Do NOT change the split (that would force re-freezing the eval set and break his own pre-registration). Change the retriever: make precedent selection class-stratified or class-contrastive — retrieve the top-1 or top-2 BM25 matches WITHIN each candidate Primary Problem class rather than top-k globally, so the model sees what an ATC-Equipment precedent and a Human-Factors precedent each look like and must choose between them, instead of seeing five votes for the prior. This also converts the flaw into the best changelog row in the submission: 'naive top-k BM25 precedent measurably worsened long-tail agreement because the exemplar pool's prior is +11pp Human Factors; class-stratified precedent fixed it' — an observed failure driving the next capability, which is exactly the shape the PDF asks for.

kill_shots.flaw: No human ceiling, and the 'panel' framing overreaches its source. I verified his quote is real — asrs.arc.nasa.gov report-processing page: 'Each report received by the ASRS is read by a minimum of two analysts.' But the same page says the two analysts' FIRST mission is hazard identification and alerting, and that classification is 'Analysts' second mission' — of the corps, not of two independent coders who reconcile a Primary Problem. Nothing on any NASA page I fetched supports 'the label was assigned by a minimum of two NASA aviation-safety analysts'. The strategy brief already flagged this exact trap for ASRS: 'one analyst label per report — you measure agreement with a single expert, not a panel.' And nowhere does the design establish an inter-analyst agreement rate.
kill_shots.why_fatal: Without a human ceiling the primary metric has no interpretable scale. If the agent lands at 58%, a judge cannot tell whether that is near-expert or terrible, because nobody knows what a second trained analyst would score against the first. That is precisely the gap micro1 closes on its own benchmarks by publishing judge-vs-hand-label agreement, and eval-set construction is what the likeliest technical judge (Andrew Maas) scrutinises hardest. Combined with the unsupported panel claim, the strongest row in the submission ('the expensive expert part was already done and paid for by the taxpayer') becomes the row a careful reader picks at.
kill_shots.fixable: Yes, and it pays for itself twice. Blind-code 25–30 eval cases himself from the narratives plus NASA's published coding form BEFORE looking at the labels, and report his own agreement with NASA as a second-reader reference — labelled honestly as a non-analyst's ceiling estimate, not a certified one. That single activity produces (a) the missing scale for the headline number, (b) the 'human time per task, compose-from-blank' arm he needs anyway at H20–21, and (c) a genuine feel for the taxonomy that will improve the SKILL.md. It replaces a weak stopwatch exercise with a measurement that does real work. Separately: reword the provenance claim to what the page actually says and stop implying a panel.

kill_shots.flaw: Zero model calls, ~26 build hours, and three capabilities all justified by unmeasured hypotheses. I confirmed the blocker is real on this machine: ANTHROPIC_API_KEY unset, no `ant` CLI, no `anthropic` SDK installed. Every corpus number he states is real — I independently recomputed 1,500 records / 1,412 distinct ACNs / 1,499 with Primary Problem / the 1354/1354 invariant / the 38.9-20.0-13.4-9.7% distribution / the 57.2% oracle-CF leave-one-out lookup, and all reproduced exactly. But every number about model behaviour is a guess.
kill_shots.why_fatal: The whole narrative — that a single prompt over-attributes to Human Factors, that precedent fixes selection errors, that the gap lives at the abstention boundary — is one unmeasured premise, and the hot take (5 pts) and the video's spine both ride on it. His own H7 gate has a branch that says 'pivot the primary metric to Contributing-Factor set F1 plus abstention' if the baseline already scores near 60%. That pivot is priced at zero hours but actually invalidates the scorer, the five buckets, the F1–F5 taxonomy, the pre-registered thresholds, both hard cases and the hot take — call it 4+ hours of rework at hour 8 of 26, with 12 hours of packaging still to come. There is also a real chance the +8pp bar is simply unreachable: the oracle-CF lookup ceiling is 57.2% even when handed the true factor set, so if a generous single prompt lands at 50%, the honest headline is a null result.
kill_shots.fixable: Only by running the baseline first, and today. Reorder the plan: get the key and run 60 cases × 1 rep of the single-prompt baseline in the first 2 hours, BEFORE building the corpus freeze, the scorer refinements, or any capability. It is ~180 short calls (narratives are small — median 393 tokens, mean 541) and costs under $3 at Opus 5 rates ($5/$25 per Mtok). That one measurement decides which metric to pre-register, which capabilities are justified, and whether the hot take survives — and it converts three predicted failure modes into observed ones, which is what the 30-point row is actually scored on. Note his ~$25 total spend estimate is optimistic by roughly 2–4× once re-runs, the 3-rep protocol, the 3-sample control and the two-stage removed experiment are counted; budget ~$100–150, which is still fine.

kill_shots.flaw: Nothing in the 26-hour plan builds the thing the analyst uses. The rubric's 20-point row asks for 'a final result the user can use, with the finish of something a person would sign their name to'. The deliverables described are records.jsonl, eval_60.jsonl, a ~40-line grader, results tables, a changelog and trajectories. The 'pre-coded draft sheet plus an explicit I-cannot-commit flag' — the actual product — is described in the pitch and appears nowhere in H0–H26. H23–25 is trajectories, H25–26 is clean-clone rehearsal.
kill_shots.why_fatal: That is a fifth of the total score resting on an artifact that is unbudgeted, and the tie-break order puts End-to-End Quality fourth precisely because judges expect it to be present, not because it is optional. A judge asking 'would the intended user consider this output high quality?' finds no output addressed to the user — only an eval harness addressed to a methodologist. It also silently weakens the human-checkpoint claim: the F3/F4 abstention gate is asserted as a design feature but nothing renders it for a human to act on, so ground rules 04/05 are answered in prose rather than in the artifact.
kill_shots.fixable: Yes, in ~2 hours, and it should come out of the trajectory budget rather than being added. A single self-contained static HTML review sheet, generated by the pipeline: one row per report, the draft Contributing Factors and Primary Problem, the evidence span highlighted inline in the narrative it came from, the ABSTAIN cases visually separated into a 'needs a human' queue, and accept/override controls. No server, no network — it opens from the clone. That is the artifact the video should walk through, and it is what makes the 'second reader, not the analyst' framing concrete instead of rhetorical.

survivable_weaknesses: Post-hoc strata selection: he chose the 9 eval sets by lowest majority-class concentration, dropping the constant-predictor floor from 39.0% corpus-wide to 27.5% on the eval pool (I reproduce 27.5%; he reports 28.3%). He publishes the criterion and the full per-set concentration table, which mitigates it — but the headline is not comparable to a random ASRS sample and he should say so in the same sentence as the number, not in a caveats section.

Split-integrity claim is overstated. 83 ACNs appear in more than one report set, and I measured that 34 of them straddle the eval/exemplar boundary (e.g. ACN 2103375 appears in cftt.pdf, ctlr.pdf AND ems.pdf). 'Overlap is exactly 0' is true only after a dedupe whose tie-break he never specifies, so the same incident genuinely lives in both topical universes and the 'no topic leaks' claim is weaker than stated. It also explains why I get 425/986 where he reports 443/969 — a ~4% difference in eval-pool membership arising purely from dedupe order. Fix in 20 minutes: assign every straddler to the exemplar pool deterministically, assert it in the test, and say so.

The input whitelist is specified at block granularity ('time, place, environment, aircraft, person, qualification, experience') but the ASRS record nests analyst-coded assessments inside those blocks. The Aircraft Component block carries a sub-field literally named 'Problem' with values {Malfunctioning 424, Failed 98, Improperly Operated 95, Design 20}. I measured that eval cases carrying an Aircraft Component block have P(Primary Problem = Aircraft) = 42.1% against a 12.2% base rate — a 3.5x lift from a partly analyst-derived field his whitelist appears to admit. Not a giveaway, but the whitelist needs to be published at field granularity with an explicit in/out decision on that field.

'Ambiguous' is a checkbox on NASA's coding form, not an act of restraint. Emitting it is predicting a 17th class, so 'abstains when the analysts did' oversells, and F3/F4 are the off-diagonal cells for one class dressed as a failure taxonomy. The metric stays honest; the tagline is what needs softening.

n=60 across 5 buckets is ~12 cases per bucket, where one case moves a bucket by 8pp, and the design specifies no confidence intervals, bootstrap, or McNemar test on the paired comparison. The +8pp headline bar may not be separable from noise. Adding a paired bootstrap CI is ~30 lines and closes the gap a benchmark-building judge will probe first.

Cost estimate is light by roughly 2–4x once 3-rep protocol, the 3-sample control, the two-stage removed experiment and inevitable re-runs are counted. Real range ~$100–150 against a stated $50 budget. Not dangerous — cost per task still lands in cents, which is the number that matters — but the budget line should be corrected before it appears in the reproduction guide.

The corpus is topic-curated, not a sample of ASRS intake ('a sampling of reports referencing X'), so the label distribution is a property of NASA's curation. He reproduces NASA's own caveat, which is the right move, but it caps generalisation and he should not let the 485-reports-per-day figure imply otherwise.

Human time per task is measured by a non-analyst on a taxonomy he wrote the manual for. He labels it honestly, which is enough — but see kill shot 3: folding it into a blind self-coding exercise turns a hollow row into a load-bearing one.

designs.candidate: Markscheme — SPF round-card generator (professional-forecaster calibration adjudication)

kill_shots.flaw: The answer-key-free verifier is structurally blind on the majority of the corpus, for the one field that matters. I read Tables 6 and 7 directly. The two invariants the design calls load-bearing — probability mass per block ~100, and claimed bin count == populated column count — discriminate SHAPE only. The design then selected its cases specifically for pairs where shape is identical and only EDGES differ: 2020Q2 vs 2024Q2 (both 11x4=44, mass 400), 1985Q1 vs 1985Q2 PRPGDP (both 6x2=12, mass 200), 2013Q4 vs 2014Q1 PRPGDP (both 10x2=20, mass 200), and 1970Q4 vs 1974Q4 vs 1975Q4 (all 15x1=15, mass 100 — yet 1970Q4's edges are 10+...<-3 from Table 6's 1968:Q4-1973:Q1 column while 1974Q4/1975Q4's are 16+...<3 from the 1974:Q4-1981:Q2 column). On roughly 10 of 15 cases the verifier cannot see a wrong bin_edges tuple at all.
kill_shots.why_fatal: The design's central engineering claim, quoted verbatim, is 'The verifier is the load-bearing piece and it needs no answer key... the data itself falsifies the claim.' That is true for bin COUNT and false for bin EDGES, and the corpus was deliberately built around count-identical/edge-different pairs. Worse, the design STATES this fact about 2020Q2/2024Q2 ('shape-based sanity checks cannot catch the substitution') as evidence the problem is hard, without noticing it is simultaneously a confession that its own headline verifier does not work on its own headline case. This is the 30-point row and the #1 published tiebreak. A judge who opens Table 7 finds it in ninety seconds, and the hot take ('the cheapest reliable verifier is an invariant the data must satisfy') is then falsified by the author's own results table.
kill_shots.fixable: Yes, ~3h, and it improves the project. Add a fifth verifier check that IS answer-key-free: require the citation to include the column-header string (e.g. '2024:Q2 to Present'), then deterministically assert the survey date falls inside the quoted header range. Date arithmetic needs no gold. Requires layout-aware extraction (see kill shot 2). Then rewrite the hot take to the stronger, honest version: 'I built the invariant verifier and here is the exact error class it structurally cannot see' — which is a better hot take than the current one and is the only one the numbers will support.

kill_shots.flaw: The verbatim-citation check is defeated by the physical layout of the very page it must police. All three modern PRGDP regimes (2024:Q2+, 2020:Q2-2024:Q1, 2009:Q2-2020:Q1) live on page 43 in three adjacent columns. I ran pypdf's extract_text() on it: the output is row-interleaved across columns — the literal first data line is '1 9.0+ 16+ 6+'. So the strings '16+', '9.0+' and '6+' all appear verbatim on page 43, and a citation of any one of them passes a verbatim-substring check no matter which regime is actually correct. Same problem on pages 40 and 42.
kill_shots.why_fatal: The design nominates this check as what makes the retrieval capability 'countable rather than anecdotal' and as the thing that means 'a fabricated citation cannot pass'. It does not stop a MISATTRIBUTED citation, which is the actual failure mode — the agent is not inventing edges, it is reading the wrong column of a real table. Capability 1 (page-addressed retrieval) therefore cannot resolve the regime for any of the three modern PRGDP cases or the 1985/2013/2014 pairs, because page-level addressing is the wrong granularity for a multi-column table. The design's whole retrieval premise is 'the governing table must be found and quoted rather than recalled' — but finding the page is not finding the column.
kill_shots.fixable:
Yes, ~2h. I confirmed pdfplumber's extract_tables() recovers page 43's structure correctly with headers intact ('2024:Q2
to
Present
(Real GDP)' as a distinct column), and extract_text(layout=True) preserves the column geometry. Switch retrieval to column-addressed (page + column header + row), and make the citation unit a (header, row, value) triple. This is a real improvement, not a patch, but it must be stated as such — the current README wording would be a false claim.

kill_shots.flaw: The gold reference already contains a transcription error of exactly the class the project exists to detect. The design says twice: 'the enumerated list of eleven exception surveys on p.38' and 'the enumerated eleven-survey exception list on p.38'. I read p.38. The list is: 1968:Q4, 1969:Q4, 1970:Q4, 1971:Q4, 1972:Q3-Q4, 1973:Q4, 1975:Q4, 1976:Q4, 1977:Q4, 1978:Q4, and 1979:Q2-Q4. That is ELEVEN COMMA-SEPARATED ENTRIES but FOURTEEN SURVEYS — 1972:Q3-Q4 is two and 1979:Q2-Q4 is three. The designer counted list items and did not expand the en-dash ranges.
kill_shots.why_fatal: This is the author's own biggest_risk ('a transcription slip becomes a scoring error that silently penalises a correct agent') manifesting in the design document, before a line of code, on the single most-cited gold artifact. If it reaches regimes.yaml, then 1972:Q3, 1979:Q2 and 1979:Q3 get the wrong target_year and a correct agent is marked wrong — silently, in a project whose entire thesis is silent wrongness. None of the three named mitigations catch it: the block-mass and populated-column invariants say nothing about target_year, and a fresh-session re-transcription only catches it if that session expands ranges the first one didn't. A judge who reads p.38 (which the README will point at) sees the project fail its own test. It is also quotable in a way that is very hard to recover from.
kill_shots.fixable: Yes, 5 minutes, and it must be done before anything else. Expand both ranges, make the exception list a 14-element set, and add a CI assertion that every en-dash range in any transcribed Fed source is expanded rather than counted. Then say so in the README as a found-and-fixed instance — turning the embarrassment into the project's best piece of evidence that hand-transcription decays exactly as claimed.

kill_shots.flaw: realised_value and the per-forecaster log scores — 2 of 6 graded fields, and the only ones that make this forecast evaluation rather than PDF lookup — are scored against the wrong data vintage, and the design misidentifies its own vintage-correct source. I opened annual-historical-values-by-survey-date-selected-variables.xlsx: its Data sheet header reads 'Annual Averages for the Year Before the Survey Year', columns (Survey Year, Survey Quarter, Real GDP, GDP Price Index), first row (1992, 1, 4848.4, 117). That file is the prior-year LEVEL BASE panelists were told to compute growth from — the denominator, not the realised outcome — and it starts at 1992Q1. So for the 8 pre-1992 cases (1970Q4, 1974Q4, 1975Q4, 1981Q2, 1981Q3, 1985Q1, 1985Q2, 1991Q4 — i.e. every hard case) the outcome falls back to current-vintage FRED, graded at +/-0.05.
kill_shots.why_fatal: Scoring a 1975 nominal-GNP density against 2026-vintage FRED GNP is a methodological error the named user would catch instantly. Benchmark revisions (1976, 1980, 1985, plus the 1991 GNP->GDP changeover) move these figures by far more than the +/-0.05 tolerance. And the fix is one curl away inside the same institution: I verified the Philadelphia Fed's Real-Time Data Research Center — the same center that runs the SPF — serves routputqvqd.xlsx (HTTP 200, 243,160 bytes, valid xlsx) with quarterly vintages. The RTDSM exists precisely to prevent this error. A macro research associate opens a 1975Q4 round card, sees a log score computed from current-vintage data, and stops trusting the artifact — which is an End-to-End-Quality failure in front of the exact reader the project names.
kill_shots.fixable: Yes, two options. Cheap (30 min): drop realised_value, log scores and PIT from the graded fields entirely, grade only the five codebook-resolution fields, and state that outcome scoring is deliberately out of scope pending real-time vintage integration. Honest and strictly better methodologically. Expensive (3-4h): vendor the RTDSM vintage files and score each round against the vintage available at the survey date. Note the cheap fix amputates the last thing making this 'forecasting' — see the framing weakness.

kill_shots.flaw: The eval-corpus derivation claim is falsified by Table 6. The design's defence against 'N=15 is small and arbitrary' is that 'the count is derived rather than chosen: the rule is one round on each side of every regime boundary the Fed itself documents, which is what produces 15 and not 10.' Applying that rule to the tables I read: Table 6 documents PRPGDP boundaries at 1973:Q1|Q2, 1974:Q3|Q4, 1981:Q2|Q3, 1985:Q1|Q2, 1991:Q4|1992:Q1, 2013:Q4|2014:Q1; Table 7 documents PRGDP boundaries at 1981:Q2|Q3, 1991:Q4|1992:Q1, 2009:Q1|Q2, 2020:Q1|Q2, 2024:Q1|Q2, and inherits Table 6's pre-1981 sub-boundaries via 'Same as PRPGDP'. The stated corpus omits the 1973:Q1/1973:Q2 boundary entirely (neither side present), omits the 'before' partners 1974:Q3, 2020:Q1 and 2024:Q1, and includes 1970:Q4, which is an interior round of 1968:Q4-1973:Q1 and not a boundary at all.
kill_shots.why_fatal: The strategy brief's single most specific judging warning is that if Andrew Maas reads it, 'eval-set construction is what gets scrutinised hardest — document provenance of each case and why it was included.' The design leads with a provenance rule that its own corpus does not follow, and each case supposedly 'carries a provenance note naming the documented change that put it there' — a note that cannot be written truthfully for 1970:Q4. Once the rule is shown to be post-hoc, 15 becomes a self-authored set where the author chose which boundaries to test, and the design loses its only defence against the N-is-small objection. The per-regime bucketing compounds it: buckets are 'pre-1981 nominal-GNP / 1981-1991 / 1992-2009 / 2009-2020 / 2020-2024 / 2024+', which collapses three genuinely different pre-1981 edge sets into one bucket.
kill_shots.fixable: Yes, ~1h, and it makes the project stronger. Either extend to the ~20 rounds the rule actually produces (adding 1973:Q1, 1973:Q2, 1974:Q3, 2020:Q1, 2024:Q1 — all of which are good cases), or drop the derivation claim and defend the 15 honestly as a stratified boundary sample with 1970:Q4 relabelled as an interior control. Also re-cut the pre-1981 reporting bucket into its three real regimes.

kill_shots.flaw: One graded field on one case has no ground truth, and the Fed says so on the page the design already cites. Page 38, immediately after the exception list: 'we are uncertain about the years referred to in the surveys of the first quarters of 1985 and 1986 and have not found documentation that can confirm our suspicion that the years do not follow the standard.' The corpus includes 1985Q1 PRPGDP, and target_year is graded with exact ==. There is no gold value to compare against — the authoritative source explicitly declines to resolve it.
kill_shots.why_fatal: In a project whose thesis is 'silently wrong because the manual is ambiguous', shipping a graded == field whose gold is an assumption the manual refuses to make is self-refuting. Either the author silently assigns the standard convention (fabricating gold, the exact sin being measured) or the case is unscoreable. It is trivially discoverable — it is two sentences below the exception list the README will quote. The design's description of 1985Q1/Q2 mentions only the bin-edge change ('same 6x2 shape, different edges' — which I confirmed is correct: 12+...<4 vs 10+...<2), showing the ambiguity was not noticed.
kill_shots.fixable: Yes, ~30 min, and this is the single best upgrade available. Make 1985Q1 the designated ABSTENTION-EXPECTED case: gold for target_year is 'unresolvable', the correct behaviour is a documented abstention citing p.38, and emitting any year is scored silently-wrong. That converts a scoring bug into the project's most persuasive case — an abstention the source itself demands — and gives the coverage guard a principled exemption. Then check 1986Q1 too.

survivable_weaknesses: The compute-matched control is structurally incapable of moving, which makes it uninformative rather than fair. Best-of-N self-consistency voting fixes STOCHASTIC error. The baseline's failure here is SYSTEMATIC — confident recall biased toward the most recent or most common bin table. Voting N times on a systematic bias returns the same wrong table N times with higher confidence. The arm will correctly report 'more compute does not help' but proves nothing about the compute hypothesis, and a sharp judge will say so. Cheap fix: state this prediction in GOOD.md before running, so the null result reads as pre-registered rather than as a control that could not have worked.

N=15 with a strict all-fields-must-match rule, reported across 6 regime buckets, puts 2-3 cases in each cell. Per-bucket reporting on n=2 is anecdote wearing a table's clothes, and the design's headline structural commitment is 'never as a single blended number'. The author concedes a 1-2 round difference is noise; 3 repeats and a bootstrap CI make the noise visible without making it smaller. Extending to ~20 cases per the fix above helps marginally, not decisively.

Licence exposure is real and ground rule 03 is a qualification gate. I confirmed philadelphiafed.org/terms-of-use returns HTTP 404 and the site footer asserts 'Copyright 2026. All rights reserved. Federal Reserve Bank of Philadelphia.' Vendoring four FRB Philadelphia files under an explicit all-rights-reserved footer with no SPDX licence is defensible but not clean. The design's handling is the most careful I have seen on this point (unmodified files, original filenames, SHA-256, attribution, refetch.py), and the Moody's BOND/BAABOND carve-out was correctly found. But there is an unresolved tension: the offline-by-default guarantee that earns the Reproducibility points is exactly what requires the redistribution. Consider shipping FRED CSVs vendored (unambiguously public domain, 17 USC 105) and the four Fed files via refetch.py with hash verification, with a documented one-command fallback.

The framing is a bait-and-switch the author has already diagnosed but not solved. 'Professional-forecaster disagreement and calibration adjudication' delivers a PDF-table-resolution benchmark. The author's own honest_self_assessment leads with this ('a documentation-comprehension benchmark wearing forecasting clothes... a partial dodge of the original brief'). Naming it first in the README is the right move and buys real credit for candour, but it does not stop a judge scanning 100 submissions from feeling misled by the title. Retitle around what it actually does — versioned-codebook resolution — and the honesty stops costing points.

The killer objection is unanswered: a researcher transcribes Tables 6, 7 and 8 once into a config and never needs the agent again. This is 13 columns of at most 20 values. The build plan itself budgets H2-H5 to do exactly that, by hand, permanently. 'The codebook keeps moving' is true but it moves roughly every five years, so the agent amortises against an afternoon of work per half-decade. The generalisation to IPUMS/NHANES/ICD-9-to-10/NAICS/HMDA is asserted and never demonstrated — the author flags this as 'the weakest joint in the argument' and is right. Cheapest credible patch: build one throwaway second instance (a single NAICS or ICD crosswalk round card) to convert the assertion into a demonstration.

The final artifact is a JSON file, but Priya owes a two-page annex on Thursday. The design is honest that the card 'is an input to Priya's judgement, not a substitute for it,' which satisfies ground rules 04/05 cleanly. But the 20-point End-to-End row asks whether the intended user would consider the output high quality, and JSON is a developer artifact. A small rendered annex — the panel table, the abstentions with reasons, the citations as footnotes — is a few hours and moves this row materially.

Human time per task is measured on 3 rounds by the person who transcribed the tables and knows where every one is. The author names this and reports min/median/max rather than a flattering point estimate, which is the right handling. It remains the weakest number in the results table and the one most likely to be challenged.

The build plan has no slack anywhere, and two blocks are classic overruns. H0-H2 asks for corpus freeze, parquet parsing of five probability sheets plus RECESS, AND a machine-checkable ledger parsed out of a 47-page errata PDF, as a CI gate. H2-H5 asks for hand transcription of three tables with page-and-quote provenance, the full deterministic scorer (log score, PIT, panel aggregate), cross-validation of every regime entry, AND three stopwatched manual scorings. Each is realistically 5-6 hours, budgeted at 2-3. Downstream, five arms x 15 cases x 3 repeats is 225 agent runs before best-of-N, whose N is sized to agent token spend and could multiply the baseline arm several-fold. Cut the errata ledger to the 5 verified sampled corrections and drop the LLM-judge arm to 15x1 if H14 arrives late.

The hot take sits in what the strategy brief identifies as the field's median lane — deterministic verification wrapped around a model, with the '- and proves it' framing appearing verbatim across a dozen competitor repos. It is well written and lands on micro1's published position, but it is not differentiating on its own. The version that IS differentiating is the inverted one forced by kill shot 1: publishing the error class the data-invariant verifier structurally cannot see.

designs.candidate: Warrant — evidence-gated defect review that publishes its own recall cost

kill_shots.flaw: The single piece of evidence offered for the gate's discriminative power is a no-op edit. I reproduced the cited case. The design says: 'on thefuck's git_push rule ... reverting only the accused line 9 flips it to False; reverting the unrelated line 13 leaves it True (correctly not attributed).' That is BugsInPy thefuck bug 5, whose bug_patch.txt is a single-hunk, one-line change touching ONLY line 9 (`and 'set-upstream' in command.output)` -> `and 'git push --set-upstream' in command.output)`). I fetched the buggy file at commit 7c858fadb3458be829d3d43666ccb46c3ed5b8a0: line 13 is `if '--set-upstream' in command_parts:`, which is byte-identical in BASE and HEAD. 'Reverting line 13 to its BASE form' writes the same bytes back. It is arithmetically guaranteed not to change behavior.
kill_shots.why_fatal: Warrant condition 3 — 'W still fails when a different changed line in the same diff is reverted instead' — is the entire claim that the gate proves LOCATION rather than mere causation by the diff. The design's only end-to-end demonstration of condition 3 does not implement condition 3; it reverts an unchanged line. So the load-bearing verification claim has zero demonstrated evidence, sitting directly under the sentence 'I verified this mechanism end to end on real code before designing around it.' A judge can check this in ninety seconds with curl. Andrew Maas-class scrutiny of eval-set construction — which the strategy brief names as the likeliest reading — finds it immediately. This is not a presentation problem; the sentence that establishes credibility is the sentence that is false.
kill_shots.fixable: Yes, cheaply, but only by weakening the claim. Re-run the demo on a multi-line fix (thefuck bug 9, 6 changed lines, or youtube-dl bug 5/23/34, 2 hunks) where a genuine second changed line exists. Cost: ~30 minutes. But see the next kill shot — fixing the demo exposes that condition 3 is inapplicable to most of the corpus.

kill_shots.flaw: Condition 3 is undefined or vacuous on the majority of the eval corpus. I applied the design's own static filter (<=2 files, no test file, <=8 changed lines) across all 78 bugs in the three chosen projects: 53 pass (youtube-dl 29, thefuck 23, PySnooper 1). Of those 53, sixteen are `lines=2 hunks=1` — a single removed line and a single added line. There is no 'different changed line in the same diff' to revert. ## KS-5 — The "empty lane" finding was a competitive census, silently promoted to a novelty claim

The strategy brief verifies *0 of 64 hackathon entries* in CVE/CVSS. True, and valuable. It says nothing about whether the problem is solved. It is close to solved, repeatedly, publicly:

| Prior art | What it is | Why it hurts |
|---|---|---|
| **CVSS-BERT** — arXiv 2111.08510 (2021) `[V]` | One BERT classifier **per CVSS metric**, concatenated into a vector, plus gradient-saliency showing **which words in the description drove each metric** | This is the design's architecture — per-metric skills + evidence spans — shipped five years ago. Reported **83.79–96.07% per-metric** and **55.3% exact-vector match** |
| **VLAI** — arXiv 2507.03607, CIRCL `[V]` | RoBERTa fine-tuned on 600k CVEs, severity band. **CC-BY-4.0, on Hugging Face, ~0.1B params (~400MB), runs offline on CPU.** Deployed in Vulnerability-Lookup | **81.58% band accuracy on the model card.** The design's CNA baseline band agreement is **48.5%**. A free, offline, vendorable model is sitting in PDF-sanctioned baseline slot #3 and the design has not run it |
| **arXiv 2504.10713** (Apr 2025) `[V]` | 31,000 CVEs, five LLM families, systematic prompt engineering | Finding: **embedding methods beat LLMs on C/I/A** — the subjective metrics. Independent confirmation of KS-3, at 200× the sample size |
| **"Fragmentation of CVSS scores in the NVD"** — *Computers & Security*, **May 2026** `[V]` | Self-described **first NVD-scale unified analysis** of cross-version coverage, **inter-source NVD-vs-CNA divergence**, and **score granularity and concentration** | "Score concentration" is the hot take's territory, measured at full NVD scale, three months before kickoff. Also reports **34.1% divergence on dual-assessed CVEs** — against the submission's 76.6%/91% |

**Why fatal.** The headline number is 26.3% exact-vector; a 2021 BERT paper reports 55.3%. Different populations — the submission evaluates on the hard divergent slice — but **no judge performs that reconciliation.** They see a 2026 agentic system posting half the number of a five-year-old encoder model and stop reading. Worse, the design cites arXiv 2512.06781 (GPT-5, 71.6% PR) as its "published weak external baseline" while CVSS-BERT reports 83.79–96.07% per-metric. Citing the weakest paper in a field of four, when a stronger one is the first search hit, reads as selective citation — and ground rule 09 is checked at the integrity screen, not the rubric.

**Fix (2 hours, and it is an *upgrade*).** Run VLAI on the 167 as a fourth arm. It is CC-BY-4.0, offline, deterministic, free, and PDF-sanctioned. Whatever it scores, the "weak baseline" charge is permanently dead — you benchmarked against a 2025 production model, not a copy-paste. Cite all four papers in a *Prior art and how this differs* section. State the population difference explicitly, in your own words, before a judge states it in theirs.

## KS-6 — The user's problem changed on 10 June 2026, and the submission is solving the old one

`[V]` **CISA BOD 26-04, "Prioritizing Security Updates Based on Risk," issued 10 June 2026.** Agency policy deadline **7 August 2026**; full implementation **7 December 2026**. It directs FCEB agencies to prioritize on four signals: **is the asset publicly exposed · is it in the KEV catalog · can exploitation be automated · does it grant total control** — with SSVC-informed remediation timelines (3/7/14/30 days). Trade coverage headline: *"From CVSS to KEV, CISA Rewrites Federal Patching Priorities."*

*(cisa.gov returns 403 to fetchers — same wall as the NVD licence page. Confirm in a browser at the same gate.)*

**Why fatal.** The pitch is: *NVD deferred 82% of her queue, so she can't triage.* But the authoritative body in the domain told that exact user, ten weeks ago, **to stop triaging on CVSS base score.** NVD's April 2026 deferral policy and CISA's June 2026 BOD are the same story from two ends: the institutions concluded that scoring every CVE is not worth doing and moved to triage-by-exploitation. The design read the first half of that story — backlog is a problem — and missed the second half, which is that **the backlog is deliberate policy, and the sanctioned remedy is not to score the queue faster.**

A judge who searches "CVE prioritization 2026" — the obvious first search for anyone auditing the problem statement — hits BOD 26-04 immediately, and the 15-point Problem & User Value row is decided against you before the agent is read. It also poisons the video's opening 40 seconds, which is where that row is actually scored.

**Fix (one paragraph, and it *strengthens* the pitch).** Own it: *"CISA just told federal agencies to stop patching by CVSS score. That is exactly why this matters — the signals BOD 26-04 names are per-asset context the analyst has and the CVE record doesn't. What she still needs from the record is the intrinsic characterisation: is this remote, does it need privileges, does it take over the box. That is the CVSS base vector, and 82% of her queue doesn't have one."* This is true, it is domain-fluent, and it converts the biggest external threat into evidence you know the field.

## KS-7 — The eval set structurally excludes every CNA whose scores are good

This is the second-order half of KS-4, and it is sharper than the tertile bias.

`[V]` NVD publishes per-CNA, per-category **acceptance levels**: **Reference (0–69.9%), Contributor (70–94.9%), Provider (95–100%)** agreement with NVD analysis. And, verbatim from `nvd.nist.gov/vuln/cvmap/Understanding-Acceptance-Levels`: **"Provider level data is considered equal to that of NVD analysis and is immediately placed into the NVD upon reception,"** audited at much lower frequency.

*(Search-snippet sourced; the page is JS-walled. Browser-confirm at the licence gate — it takes 30 seconds and it is load-bearing.)*

**The consequence.** Eligibility for the eval pool is "carries both an NVD Primary and a CNA Secondary vector." For Provider-level CNAs, NVD largely does **not** produce a second vector — the CNA's goes straight in. So the pool is conditioned on **the CNA being one NVD does not fully trust.** Divergence is inflated by construction. That is very likely why the pool shows ~91% divergence while the 2026 *Computers & Security* paper reports 34.1% across dual-assessed CVEs.

**Why fatal, on three counts:**

1. **The baseline number is a misstatement of the user's experience.** "The shipped vector is exact 9.0% of the time" is presented as what the analyst gets today. It is what she gets *from the vendors NVD audits most*. Her real queue includes Provider CNAs whose vectors match NVD ≥95% of the time. Stacked on KS-4's fastest-analysed bias, both selection effects push the same direction — making the starting point look weak. That is the "baseline set up to fail" pattern twice over, and it is now *structural*, not a window choice.
2. **Deployment inversion.** An agent tuned where the CNA is wrong 91% of the time will over-override in production, where most CNA vectors are fine. That is a concrete, nameable harm from the eval design — the exact species of finding micro1's own cited literature (arXiv 2507.02825, seven of ten benchmarks violating task validity) trains its people to hunt.
3. **A judge can check the direction in one query** by looking at the assigner mix of your pool against the cvmap tables.

**Fix (~20 min of joining, and it is the best single robustness result available to this project).** You already hold each eval case's assigner. Join against the published acceptance levels and report APY/DUR **stratified by acceptance level**. Falsifiable prediction: your pool skews Reference/Contributor. If it does, you have measured your own selection bias with a pre-existing human-derived label and can state a bound. If it doesn't, you have killed the objection outright. Either outcome is a win, and it costs less than half an hour.

## KS-8 — The deterministic verifier verifies nothing that can be wrong

The strategy brief's stated reason to pick this lane: *"the score is a closed-form formula, so a deterministic verifier can mechanically reject any vector whose stated score doesn't match. Verification becomes load-bearing, not decorative."*

Interrogate that. The agent's output is a **vector**. The score is a **pure function of the vector**. So the verifier can only catch a disagreement between the agent's vector and the agent's *self-reported* score — which never occurs if you simply compute the score from the vector instead of asking the model for it. Either the design asks the model for a redundant number so the verifier has something to catch (theatre), or the verifier catches nothing. Everything else it does — legal enum values, well-formed vector string — is a JSON schema, which structured output already enforces.

**Why fatal.** Reproducing 4,380/4,380 published scores proves your formula implementation is correct. It does **not** make verification load-bearing. A wrong-but-well-formed vector passes every check. Agent Solution & Engineering is 30 points and tie-break #1, and micro1's job specs name *deterministic verification* as a literal hiring criterion — these are people who build verifiers for a living. They will see a correctly-implemented calculator presented as a safety mechanism.

**Fix — and this is where the project's one genuinely novel idea is hiding.** Make the verifier decide something. When the agent abstains on *k* metrics, enumerate every legal combination of those metrics (AV 4 × AC 2 × PR 3 × UI 2 × S 2 × C/I/A 3 each — ≤27 combinations for k=3), compute min and max base score, and check whether they fall in the same severity band. If they do, **the band is determined regardless of how the abstained metrics resolve** — and you can ship it. That is closed-form, brute-forceable, deterministic, genuinely load-bearing, useful to a practitioner (*"I don't know PR, but it's HIGH either way"*), and I could not find it published anywhere. It is also the frame that finally makes DUR sound: report under-rating against the band the agent **guarantees**, not against a point estimate.

## KS-9 — The architecture generates no trajectory worth reading, and trajectories are the gate item

Deliverable 04 asks for representative trajectories showing *"what the agent did and how its tools responded … the feedback that shaped its next step … any retries or human checkpoints."* `[V]` micro1 pays $2–15 per trace for this and staffs a standing $80–100/hr role curating it. It is the deliverable closest to their commercial interest and the one the contestant has never produced.

A fan-out of 8 stateless per-metric classifications produces **8 near-identical traces in which nothing is fed back, nothing is retried, and nothing is checkpointed.** There is no next step to shape. The architecture is structurally incapable of producing an interesting trajectory — and simultaneously reads as the component inflation the PDF penalises by name. KS-3's advice to cut to 3 skills helps the point count; it does not create a narrative.

The trace worth selling is: *retrieve precedent → precedents conflict → verifier proves the band is undetermined → abstain and route to a human, citing the specific sentence it could not resolve.* That trace only exists if abstention is the mechanism rather than a side-channel.

## What breaks on the judge's machine (concrete, Windows-origin)

- **The SHA256 manifest is a CRLF bomb.** Vendored JSON hashed on a Windows checkout, cloned on macOS/Linux without `.gitattributes` forcing `-text`/`binary`, yields different bytes — and the **first command in your reproduction guide prints FAIL.** Your flagship integrity artifact becomes a "this doesn't reproduce" message. Add `* -text` for `data/**` and verify with a fresh clone on a second path before you sleep Sunday.
- **The 150MB precedent index may be unpushable.** GitHub hard-rejects files >100 MiB and warns above 50 MiB. Discovering this at hour 65 with a single-file JSONL index is a deadline-day catastrophe; LFS "fixes" it by breaking the offline clone. Shard it, gzip it, or field-prune it **now**, and do a throwaway push test today.
- **"Runs offline" is true of the harness and false of the agent.** The agent needs an API key and network. If the README says "offline, no network, no account" without splitting tiers, the judge who actually runs the agent arm hits a wall on the row you are counting on. Say it in two lines: *Tier 1 — replay committed run artifacts, offline, deterministic, 90s. Tier 2 — live re-run, needs `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, ~$X, ~Y min.*
- **Python floor.** `hashlib.file_digest`, `datetime.UTC`, `tomllib` are all 3.11+. Pin and state the floor.

**First screen.** The working title is nine words of jargon. A judge at an agent-eval company is not a vulnerability manager; they do not know what CVE enrichment is. Compare the PDF's own example framing: *"a team considering the purchase of a private repository."* A person and a stake. ## The single change that most raises the odds

**Replace exact-vector agreement with a selective metric: per-metric decisions auto-settled correctly, at a pre-registered wrong-auto-accept budget — abstention gated on NVD's own published per-CNA acceptance level plus precedent purity — and publish the full risk–coverage curve.**

One move, and it defuses almost everything above:

- **A one-line constant cannot beat it.** Constants have no confidence signal; they occupy a single point on the coverage axis. The agent produces a curve. Compare at matched coverage. **KS-1 dies structurally**, not by raising a threshold.
- **The LLM stops being asked the questions it loses.** Prior art says it degrades PR and A; under a gate it abstains there instead of overriding. **KS-3 is contained by design, not by hope.**
- **It claims the lane the brief verified as empty** — abstention as the *primary* metric, 0 occupancy — which this design was already paying for and not claiming.
- **The confidence signal is a pre-existing human-derived label**, published by NVD, not model self-report and not an LLM judge. Hard constraint 1 is satisfied more strongly than before, and the design's failed deterministic trigger (8.7/15.4/6.2/8.3%) gets replaced by one *defined* as historical agreement with the label source.
- **KS-4 and KS-7 become the subject instead of the caveat**: the eval set is the distrusted-CNA, fastest-triaged slice — which is precisely the slice where routing to a human is the right answer.
- **KS-8's verifier becomes load-bearing** via band-invariance over the abstained metrics.
- **KS-9 gets its trace**: conflict → proof of undetermined band → abstain with a cited span.
- **The numbers become legible.** Per-metric decisions live in the 65–95% range — not saturated, not floor-scraping — and 167 CVEs × 8 decisions is a richer evidence base than 167 all-or-nothing vectors. Report per-metric, never the mean; micro1's own published methodology rejects blended numbers.
- **The cost table flips.** The win is analyst minutes routed away from decisions the machine settled, not pennies of tokens.

Do it **before** the agent exists. Afterwards it is indistinguishable from moving the goalposts.
